evidence: Cic. Div. 2.144: celeritās et vīs equōrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word, of bodies, ships, news and minds (celeritās ingeniī). At full speed: quam celerrimē (Caes. B.G. 1.37.4) or summā celeritāte.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.107: aliōs vidēmus vēlōcitāte ad cursum … valēre
Cic. Tusc. 4.31: vēlōcitās corporis celeritās appellātur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Speed of running and moving, of the body (Cicero, Caesar); of the mind only after Augustus (Lewis & Short). Traupman’s speed limit is vēlōcitātis modus (see limit).

phrases.latin: nōn vīribus aut vēlōcitāte aut celeritāte corporum rēs magnae geruntur, sed cōnsiliō, auctōritāte, sententiā
phrases.english: great things are not done by strength or speed or quickness of body, but by planning, authority and judgement

phrases.latin: cancrī in pavōre et retrōrsī parī vēlōcitāte redeunt
phrases.english: when frightened, crabs run back, backwards, just as fast

phrases.latin: Etiam celeritās in dēsīderiō mora est.
phrases.english: When you long for something, even speed is slow.

phrases.latin: rē frūmentāriā quam celerrimē potuit comparātā magnīs itineribus ad Ariovistum contendit
phrases.english: he got the corn supply together as fast as he could and marched at full stretch against Ariovistus
